subject: Draft RACI + retention & logging requirements — post-demo recap
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@medlytics.com>, procurement@medlytics.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft RACI + retention & logging requirements — post-demo recap

Hi Elena / MedLytics team,

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — appreciate the time. Per our call, Im sending a first-pass RACI + requirement sketch for the MAP milestone focused on data handling, retention, and logging. This is intentionally lightweight so we can converge quickly.

Key points from the call:
- MedLytics will handle PHI ingestion at edge and expects Redwood to never persist raw PHI beyond session context (exceptions negotiable under BAA).
- Required audit logs: per-request headers, model variant served, latency, token counts, and user identifier mapping (pseudonymized).
- Target retention windows: short-term logs 30 days, aggregated telemetry 12 months, and full audit trail (redacted) retainable for up to 36 months depending on legal/clinical needs.

Attached: MAP_RACI_v0.1.xlsx (draft), retention-logging-summary.pdf (notes).

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Elena: confirm whether MedLytics requires us to store any PHI-derived embeddings or if those must be treated as PHI and purged within 24 hours.
2) Rishi: can you draft a short note on encryption-at-rest and key-management options we can offer in Private deployment?
3) Monica/Karthik: please comment on proposed RACI rows in tab 2 of the attached (ownership, SLA target, evidence needed).

Proposed target close for this milestone: 2027-04-15 (aligns to legal + security review). If that timeline is realistic, well reflect it in the MAP.

Thanks,
Irene

--
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: MAP_RACI_v0.1.xlsx (spreadsheet), retention-logging-summary.pdf (summary)
From: Elena Martinez <elena@medlytics.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medlytics.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft RACI + retention & logging requirements — post-demo recap

Irene,

Thanks for the recap and the materials. A few clarifications from our side:

- PHI / embeddings: We cannot allow raw PHI to be stored by vendors. We are comfortable with pseudonymized embeddings that cannot be traced back to a patient without a separate key held by MedLytics. So: embeddings are acceptable only if they are deterministically hashed with a MedLytics-only salt and keys are customer-controlled.
- Retention windows: 30 days for request-level logs is fine, but for clinical audit we will likely request on-demand exports up to 7 years (archival) — we understand that may be export-only and stored in our bucket. Please note this will create a dependency on our S3 archival policy.
- Audit evidence: SOC2 type II report and evidence of logging schema are needed for procurement. Can you confirm timelines for providing SOC2 artifacts and a sample audit log schema?

Procurement note: well need a short note from Redwood confirming no raw PHI retention by default and whether Private deployment can support customer KMS.

Happy to meet mid-week if helpful.

Best,
Elena

--
Elena Martinez
Head of Platform Security, MedLytics
elena@medlytics.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Martinez <elena@medlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft RACI + retention & logging requirements — post-demo recap

Irene / team / Elena,

Quick technical answers to Elenas asks:

- KMS / key ownership: Private deployment supports BYOK (customer KMS/HSM). Hosted can be configured with customer-managed keys in select regions (needs add-on). Will confirm exact vendors supported (AWS KMS/GCP KMS/HashiCorp Vault).
- PHI embeddings: We can implement deterministic hashing + HMAC with customer salt on ingest; however, that will impact dedup and retrieval accuracy. Option: keep ephemeral embeddings in memory for inference path and only persist aggregated/hashed vectors to a customer-owned storage endpoint.
- Logging schema: Ive attached a one-page sample (see retention-logging-summary.pdf) with field-level names and example events. We log: timestamp, request_id, model_variant, token_count_in, token_count_out, latency_ms, user_pseudonym_id, request_hash. For PHI-sensitive routes we can suppress certain fields or redact values before persisting.

Risk / dependency notes:
- Export dependency: If MedLytics requests 7-year archival, well rely on their S3 retention & export policies; Redwood can provide the export tooling but wont host 7y archives in Hosted by default.
- Evidence: SOC2 Type II artifacts: security@redwood.com can provide the report once a redaction/engagement letter is in place. I will coordinate with Security to get a redacted copy by 2027-03-29.

Ill add inline comments to the MAP_RACI_v0.1.xlsx with proposed owners for each row (Security = Rishi, Account = Irene/Monica, Legal = Karthik).

-Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@medlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, procurement@medlytics.com
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft RACI + retention & logging requirements — post-demo recap

Elena / team,

Thanks for the rapid replies — below is an action-oriented summary and the proposed RACI captured inline (Ive also updated the spreadsheet in the Drive link). If were aligned, Ill mark the MAP milestone with a target close of 2027-04-15 and route the SOC2 evidence request to security.

Summary & assignments (RACI highlights):
- Requirement: No raw PHI persisted by Redwood by default; customer-held key for pseudonymization/embedding salt.
  - Responsible: MedLytics (ingest salt + KMS)
  - Accountable: MedLytics / Procurement for legal requirements
  - Consulted: Redwood Security (Rishi) on redaction options
  - Informed: Redwood account team (Irene / Monica)

- Requirement: Request-level logs retained 30 days in Hosted; on-demand export to customer archive (S3) for long-term retention (up to 7y).
  - Responsible: Redwood (export tooling) + MedLytics (archive policy)
  - Accountable: Redwood Engineering / MedLytics Ops

- Requirement: Audit evidence (SOC2 Type II + sample log schema).
  - Responsible: Redwood Security (provide redacted report)
  - Deliverable ETA: 2027-03-29 (Rishi to confirm)

Open items / dependencies:
- MedLytics to confirm whether any embeddings will be classified as PHI (if yes, require purge-within-24h).
- Procurement: confirm contract clause language for retention/export and BAA expectations (we can propose language).
- Legal review if special clinical audit export obligations apply (may push milestone timeline).

Next steps / meetings:
- Rishi will deliver SOC2 redacted copy and update the Drive by 2027-03-29.
- Elena / procurement to confirm embedding classification by 2027-04-01.
- Proposed MAP milestone close: 2027-04-15 (to be updated in MAP once the above are confirmed).

If that looks good, Elena, please reply with explicit "ACK" and any edits to the assignments. Monica / Karthik: please review the RACI tab and flag any ownership edits.

Best,
Irene

--
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
